claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows two drive shafts with rubber CV boots.
Photo 0 shows a steering rack leaning against a wall.
Photo 0 shows a car radiator on the right side.
Photo 0 shows a starter motor on the ground.

claims.claim: Sold as is, for parts, repair or recycling
claims.evidence: The visual condition of grease and rust supports a 'used' state, but the intent to sell for scrap is a seller statement.

risks.proof: Clear photos of part numbers, manufacturer stamps, or the donor vehicle's VIN plate.
risks.if_unproven: as generic scrap metal by weight.

risks.risk: Radiator or steering rack may have internal leaks or blockages.
risks.proof: A video of a pressure test or a fluid flow test.
risks.if_unproven: as leaking/damaged units for recycling only.

risks.risk: Starter motor may have a burnt solenoid or failed motor.
risks.proof: A video of a bench test showing the gear engaging and spinning when powered.
risks.if_unproven: as a non-functional core for rebuilding.

risks.risk: CV joints may be worn, clicking, or seized despite intact boots.
risks.proof: A video showing the shafts being rotated by hand to check for smooth movement and lack of play.

risks.risk: Brake caliper piston may be seized or seals perished.
risks.proof: A video showing the piston compressing and extending under air pressure.
risks.if_unproven: as a seized unit for scrap.

proof_requests: Close-up photos of any part numbers or brand markings on all items.
The make, model, and year of the car these parts were removed from.
A video showing the starter motor being tested with a battery.
Photos of the radiator inlets/outlets to check for corrosion or blockage.
response.reason: The items are clearly identified by the witness and the seller explicitly describes them as scrap or for parts. They can be priced at their worst-case value as scrap metal or cores for rebuilding.
